messages:
maya: paging oncall — seeing sustained 5xx spike for EU region, traffic spilling to fallbacks. Affects premium and standard routes. graphs: https://console.redwood.ai/graphs/incident/1794500123
incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-1794500123 (P1) — page sent to oncall-uk and sven. Runbook: region-spillover.
oncall-uk: taking. quick ask — is this a capacity exhaust or routing decision flip?
maya: initial hypothesis is capacity in eu-west pool exhausted causing router to pick fallback models in us-west. error signature is `rpc_timeout` + `kv_cache_miss` on generation.
sven: I see matching traces in the router: `route_decision: fallback` entries up since 12:22:11 UTC. sample log: `2026-03-15T12:22:15Z router[eu]: route_id=abc123 user_tier=premium reason=pool_full fallback=model-global-small`
lucy: adding monitoring graphs — latency P95 up from 180ms -> 1.2s for eu requests, error rate +380%. Also increased cross-region egress to us-west.
diego: pulling scheduler metrics — eu-west GPU pool at 98% util for the last 8 minutes; autoscaler not adding nodes because `scale_block: budget_check_fail`. config shows monthly commit limit hit for dedicated capacity.
maya: copy of router policy snippet (from config store):
```
route_policy: tiered-fallback-v3
rules:
  - match: region == eu-west
    preferred: model-eu-1
    fallback: model-global-small
    fallback_priority: [model-eu-proxy, model-global-small]
  - match: user_tier == premium
    override: prefer model-eu-pro-1
```

sven: interesting — the router picks `model-global-small` when both `model-eu-proxy` and `model-eu-1` report high load. Looking at router logs there's a bug where `prefer` list is reversed in the runtime cache, so the fallback comparator uses capacity ascending instead of descending.
aj_t: can you paste the specific router decision log lines?
sven: sure — snippet: `2026-03-15T12:22:14Z router: decision=[candidate=model-global-small score=0.12 reason=lowest_latency_estimate] trace_id=...` and `2026-03-15T12:22:14Z router: candidate=model-eu-1 score=0.78 reason=overloaded`. But the next log shows `selector: pick candidate with min(score)` which is inverted logic.
lucy: so the router is choosing the lowest score but the scoring function is inverse (lower means worse). That would cause misroutes to small global variants.
diego: that matches customer reports — premium customers hit lower-capacity models and saw quality regressions. I pulled a couple of request payloads where `model_id` returned `model-global-small` despite `user_tier=premium`.
maya: customer impact: 8 active customers affected, most in EU, a few API errors causing 4xx/5xx for 3 customers (support tickets opened).
monitoring-bot: Alert: 5xx_rate_eu increased to 12% (threshold 1%). Pager duty: 3 pages sent.
aj_t: immediate mitigation options: (1) temporarily pin premium -> model-eu-1 via routing override, (2) bump autoscaler lower threshold to add nodes, (3) fix selector comparator and roll runtime patch. Which do we do now?
oncall-uk: short term: pin premium to model-eu-1 for 15m and force fallback order to prefer `model-eu-proxy` before global. That avoids quality regression. Medium: bump autoscaler to scale sooner. Long: patch comparator in router runtime and add unit test.
sven: I can craft a hotfix for the comparator but it's a runtime change — needs canary. prefer immediate config override.
maya: agree. I'll apply a routing override to pin `user_tier=premium` -> `model-eu-1` via console.
deploy-bot: Received config update request: apply override `route_override/premium-pin` by maya. Requesting approval.
aj_t: approve. :thumbsup:
maya: applying now. CLI: `redwood routes apply --name premium-pin --match 'user_tier==premium && region==eu-west' --force-model model-eu-1 --ttl 900`
deploy-bot: Override applied successfully. Rolling to all router instances in eu-west (canary 10%).
monitoring-bot: Metric: premium_eu_fallback_rate down 60% within 60s of override. 5xx_rate trend flattening.
lucy: customers still seeing higher latency but no more model-quality regressions in samples. support notes: three tickets, two acknowledged impacted tokens, one temporary failure.
diego: autoscaler change — we bumped min_replicas in eu-west pool from 6 -> 8 to avoid immediate re-trigger. CLI: `infra autoscaler update --pool eu-west --min 8` (applied).
sven: filed runtime bug: https://issues.redwood.ai/INC-1794500123-rt-bug — comparator flips sign when `prefer` list length >1. I'll attach regression test.
maya: timeline so far: 12:22 root cause begins (pool saturates) -> 12:23 router starts misrouting -> 12:24 pages sent -> 12:25 override applied -> 12:26 autoscaler adjusted -> 12:29 visible improvement. Need to collect full logs for RCA.
aj_t: actions for in-RCA: 1) collect router decision traces for 12:15-12:30 UTC (sven), 2) full autoscaler history (diego), 3) list of affected customers + request ids (support + maya), 4) config store snapshot (lucy), 5) replay synthetic load against patched comparator (sven).
oncall-uk: I'll do post-incident customer comms template. Also recommending temporary increase to reserved capacity for eu for next 30d.
monitoring-bot: Followup: CPU/GPU metrics show autoscaler hit budget check failure at 12:20 due to commit cap. Debt ticket created: INC-1794500123-budget-cap-review.
aj_t: ok team — let's keep this thread for the RCA artifact. Save all logs and paste timeline. We'll schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 UTC. If anyone finds other hypotheses (config drift, routing cache TTL), post here.
lucy: attaching sample request ids that triggered fallback: `req: 5f8a2c, 5f8a2d, 5f8a2f` (pasted to incident storage).
sven: temp root cause hypothesis for RCA: invert comparator bug + autoscaler budget cap => misrouting + inability to scale. Priority fixes: runtime comparator patch (high), autoscaler audit (medium), add canary config validation for `prefer` ordering (low).
maya: thanks all. I'm going to open the RCA doc and paste this thread. linking: https://docs.redwood.ai/rca/INC-1794500123
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1794500123 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Transitioning to RCA collection.
aj_t: good work. Closing paging loop. Keep updates to this thread only.
